subject: Re: Access controls & support access - follow-up from today's call
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Hart <alice.hart@fintrust.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Access controls & support access - follow-up from today's call

Hi Alice — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and a few follow-ups on access controls so we can scope the security review and demo next week.

Key points we captured on the call:
- RBAC: FinTrust needs role-based restrictions so engineers cannot access production customer data; roles include Admin, App Engineer, Support Agent, Auditor.
- Least privilege: Support sessions should grant ephemeral access scoped to specific resources and time-boxed.
- Support access / break-glass: You mentioned a documented break-glass procedure for urgent investigations with audit logging. Can you confirm who owns approvals today?
- Data residency: Primary tenant in us-east-1 and requirement that PII never leave region for processing.
- Logging/monitoring: Need tamper-evident audit logs for support sessions and tokenized request traces for debugging.

Ask: could you share any internal access control matrix or a short requirements doc? If you can send that (even a summary PDF), we’ll map Redwood's controls to each item and return a concise checklist before the tech deep-dive.

Next steps I propose:
1) You share the access requirements doc (if available).
2) We provide a 1-2 page mapping (RBAC, support access flow, break-glass, audit logs).
3) Tech deep-dive Tues 6/30 10:00am PT — confirm?

Attached: "FinTrust-IT-Access-Requirements.pdf" (per your note during the call).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Alice Hart <alice.hart@fintrust.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: IT Security <security@fintrust.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 18:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Access controls & support access - follow-up from today's call

Marissa — thanks for the recap and the clear next steps. Attaching the internal matrix we referenced. High-level answers inline below and in the attachment.

- RBAC: We currently have role definitions and an access matrix; enforcement is via our IAM and some application-level checks. Admin role is limited to two SREs; Support Agent role is scoped to customer support sandbox plus ephemeral access to prod when approved.
- Least privilege: Approvals are handled via our on-call manager and require a ticket (Jira) plus manager signoff for prod.
- Break-glass: We use a push-button escalation for incident response; after action we run a post-mortem and permanently log the session. Approval owner: "On-call Manager" (team@fintrust.com).
- Data residency: All PII processing must remain in us-east-1; backups in DR region are encrypted and access-controlled.
- Logs: We retain audit logs 7 years; security asks for immutable storage and integrity checks.

See attached: FinTrust-IT-Access-Requirements.pdf (matrix and current procedures). Happy to join the tech call tomorrow.

Regards,
Alice Hart
Director, IT Security
FinTrust
alice.hart@fintrust.com

Attachment: FinTrust-IT-Access-Requirements.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Hart <alice.hart@fintrust.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Access controls & support access - follow-up from today's call

Hi Alice — thanks for the matrix. Attached is a short mapping doc and our proposed next steps for the tech call. Summary highlights:

- RBAC: Redwood supports tenant-scoped roles (Admin, Engineer, Support, Auditor). Role enforcement enforced at API layer and runtime; we can map FinTrust roles 1:1.
- Support access & ephemeral tokens: We issue time-limited support tokens tied to a support session id; tokens expire automatically and are scoped to specific customer resources. Sessions are recorded and tied to the ticket id.
- Break-glass: Proposed flow — engineer requests via Jira -> on-call manager approves (PagerDuty ack) -> support token issued for X hours -> all actions logged to immutable audit store -> post-incident review and permanent log retention.
- Logging: Audit logs are write-once (append-only) and stored encrypted with integrity checks; retention configurable up to 7+ years. We can provide an auditor export in CSV/JSON for compliance reviews.
- Data residency: Confirmed all runtime processing for FinTrust customers will be in us-east-1; backups follow encrypted DR flow and are access-controlled.

Attachments: "Redwood-Access-Controls-SLA.pdf" and "Access-controls-mapping-FT-4891.pdf" (the mapping).

Next steps:
1) Confirm the tech-call time: are you OK for 10:00am PT today?
2) If FinTrust wants any changes to the break-glass approvers or retention windows, highlight them in the call and we'll capture formal exceptions in the SOW.

If you want, we can also loop in our Security Engineer (David) for the part of the call that covers audit/export details.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
